maria (infra): Heads-up: planning a maintenance window for APAC satellite pool (saturn-pool). NIC firmware + kernel micropatch. Target Tue 02:00-04:00 JST. We'll do 6 cohorts (~10 nodes / cohort) rolling drains. Posting runbook + canary plan here.

devin: Which cohort ordering? any capacity reservations for hosted?

maria (infra): Cohorts ordered by affinity: saturn-a..f to minimize cross-az egress. We'll drain low-traffic cohorts first (a->f). Hosted customers will be routed to EU/US fallback if capacity drops; dedicated tenants remain on pinned capacity where applicable. Expect short capacity pressure windows (~5–10m) per cohort.

sarah (oncall): Last time we saw KV cache cold-starts cause a latency spike for seq=128 prompts. What's the warmup plan?

maria (infra): Planned warmbackfill + prefix warmup after each cohort drain. Job: `scripts/warmup-prefix --pool saturn-pool --cohort $i --parallel 5`

maria (infra): Drain command (manual ops step):
```
kubectl drain node/saturn-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
# then cordon, run host-evac checks
```

ops-bot: Scheduled maintenance created: MNT-2026-042-apac-saturn (starts 8101234567).

leo (finance): If traffic routes to EU/US briefly, egress spend will tick up. Rough estimate +0.6–1.2% monthly run rate if window hits peak. Can we use reserved burst capacity in APAC instead to avoid cross-region egress?

maria (infra): We have a small reserved burst pool for emergencies — plan is: prefer local reserved burst up to 100 GPUs, then fallback cross-region. Finance impact should be minimal; will keep you posted if we exceed burst.

ashok (eng-runtime): Suggest adding a routing policy to prefer quantized model variants during cohort drains (q8/q4) to reduce GPU memory and throughput pressure. Easy to flip in the router.

maria (infra): Good call. We'll add a temporary routing rule: if saturn-pool util > 75% then prefer model_variant:q8 with soft-fallback. I'll attach the policy snippet in the runbook.

redwood-monitor: Alert suppression window set for saturn-pool maintenance 02:00-04:00 JST.

tim (sre): I'll own canary validation. Proposed two-step canary: 1) single-node cohort drain + smoke tests, 2) proceed to full rolling cohorts. Smoke tests:
- median p95 latency < 200ms for 128-token generation
- KV cache hit rate > 70% within 10m after warmup
- no 5xx > 0.5% sustained

maria (infra): Agreed. Canaries will run for 20m after warmup. If any test fails, we abort and rollback with auto-un-drain.

devin: Can you post exact cohort schedule here? Need to coordinate support shift.

maria (infra): Schedule (JST):
- Cohort A: 02:00 — 02:15 (canary)
- Cohort B: 02:30 — 02:45
- Cohort C: 03:00 — 03:15
- Cohort D: 03:30 — 03:45
- Cohort E: 03:55 — 04:10
- Cohort F: 04:20 — 04:35
(we'll keep small gaps for warmbackfill; final end depends on canary outcome)

sarah (oncall): I'll be paged if p95 > 350ms or error rate > 1% during the window. Please tag me in the runbook.

leo (finance): FYI: if we use cross-region fallback > 20 minutes total, please file a short post-window cost note. I'll review charges.

ashok (eng-runtime): Also recommend pre-warming the router rule for q8 a few minutes before cohort A to reduce decision flapping.

maria (infra): Will do. Pre-warm steps in runbook.

tim (sre): Small ops checklist reminder:
1) snapshot telemetry dashboards
2) set alert suppression with thresholds
3) ensure disaster rollback playbook ready (`runbook/rollback-un-drain.sh`)

maria (infra): I'll push final comm to #support and status page 6 hours before. Ops oncall, please stand by at 01:45 JST.

devin: :thumbsup: noted.

maria (infra): Post-mortem expectations: capture KV hit regression, latency delta, and any cost deltas. If all green, we'll reuse this pattern for other satellite pools.

redwood-monitor: Maintenance MNT-2026-042-apac-saturn acknowledged by 7 services.
